about: Synthetic test data (no real studies, people or organisations). Does the judge transfer beyond AI? Seven fields, six items each, written in each field's own vocabulary rather than the judge's: three credible (a careful study, a careful news report, an honest null or negative result) and three not (a hype press release, a small study that overclaims, a calm post that cites nothing). Labels: credible true/false. Written by the same person who wrote the judge, so it tests vocabulary transfer, not independent ground truth; human labels on real pieces are the real test (see /m/labels).

items.title: Sample: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of drug S in adults with mild hypertension (test data)
items.text: We randomly assigned 1,204 patients to drug S or placebo in a 1:1 ratio at 31 sites; the trial was preregistered before enrollment. After 12 weeks, systolic blood pressure fell by 9.1 mmHg with drug S and 3.4 mmHg with placebo (difference 5.7 mmHg; 95% CI, 4.2 to 7.2). Adverse events were similar between groups. Limitations include the short follow-up and the exclusion of patients with kidney disease; the trial was not powered to detect differences in cardiovascular events.

items.title: Sample: Blood pressure pill shows modest benefit in large trial (test data)
items.text: A trial of 1,204 adults, published this week in a medical journal (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.001), found that the pill lowered blood pressure by about 6 points more than a placebo over three months. The researchers say the study was too short to show whether it prevents heart attacks or strokes, and patients with kidney disease were not included. Independent doctors said the effect is real but modest, and it remains unclear whether it beats existing drugs that were not compared in this study.

items.title: Sample: Supplement V did not reduce respiratory infections in older adults: a randomized trial (test data)
items.text: In this preregistered trial, 2,350 participants aged 65 or older were randomized to supplement V or placebo for one year. Infections occurred in 18.2% and 18.9% of participants respectively (hazard ratio 0.96; 95% CI 0.81 to 1.13; p = 0.62). Supplement V did not reduce infections. Adherence was 84% in both groups. The results may not generalize to people with low baseline levels, who were few in our sample.

items.title: Sample: Revolutionary miracle compound reverses aging, company announces (test data)
items.text: Sample Bio today announced a revolutionary breakthrough that will change medicine forever. Its proprietary compound reverses aging and rejuvenates every cell in the body. Early users report feeling twenty years younger. This is the most important discovery in human history and the age of disease is over. Pre-orders open next month.

items.title: Sample: Herbal extract H cures chronic migraine (test data)
items.text: We gave herbal extract H to 9 patients with chronic migraine. All patients reported fewer headaches after two weeks. These results prove that extract H cures chronic migraine and should become the first-line treatment for all migraine sufferers worldwide.

items.title: Sample: Why cholesterol doesn't matter anymore (test data)
items.text: Cholesterol is already irrelevant to heart health, and every cardiologist secretly knows it. Within a few years the guidelines will be thrown out entirely. Most of what you were told about diet is wrong, and the evidence keeps piling up in one direction. Soon nobody will measure cholesterol at all. The old model is collapsing and each new year makes it more obvious. The shift is inevitable.

items.title: Sample: Observed warming of the upper ocean, 2005 to 2025, from a float network (test data)
items.text: Using measurements from 3,800 autonomous floats, we estimate that the upper 2,000 m of the ocean gained heat at a rate of 0.62 ± 0.08 W per square metre over 2005 to 2025. We compare this with three independent reanalysis products and find agreement within uncertainty. The estimate is less certain in polar regions and marginal seas, where float coverage is sparse. Data and processing scripts are openly available in a public archive.

items.title: Sample: Ocean heat rising steadily, float data show (test data)
items.text: A new study (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.002) using data from about 3,800 ocean floats found the upper ocean has kept warming at a steady rate over the past 20 years, matching three other independent estimates. The authors caution that coverage near the poles is thin, so the numbers there are less certain. Scientists not involved said the result fits earlier work, though whether the rate is speeding up remains an open question.

items.title: Sample: No detectable trend in regional hail frequency, 1980 to 2024 (test data)
items.text: We analysed 44 years of hail reports and radar records from 212 stations. After correcting for changes in reporting practice, we find no statistically significant trend in hail frequency (trend 0.3% per decade; 95% CI, -1.1 to 1.7). A trend in hail size may exist but our data cannot resolve it. Limitations include inconsistent reporting before 1995.

items.title: Sample: New device ends climate change for good (test data)
items.text: Sample Climate Co. has unveiled a game-changing machine that will single-handedly reverse global warming. This unprecedented technology captures all the carbon in the air and the climate crisis is officially solved. Investors are calling it the greatest invention of the century. Nothing will ever be the same.

items.title: Sample: Backyard sensor proves the region is cooling (test data)
items.text: We installed one temperature sensor in a backyard and recorded readings for three weeks in autumn. Temperatures fell steadily throughout the period. This demonstrates that the region is cooling and that global warming has reversed.

items.title: Sample: The grid will run itself by 2030 (test data)
items.text: Renewables are already cheaper than everything else, and the grid will run entirely on them within a few years. Storage is a solved problem now, and every utility is quietly switching over. Each new year compounds the trend. Fossil fuels will vanish from the grid soon, and anyone who doubts it simply hasn't been paying attention. It is inevitable.

items.title: Sample: Superconductivity at 29 K in a layered nitride under ambient pressure (test data)
items.text: We synthesised 14 samples of a layered nitride and measured resistance and magnetic susceptibility. Zero resistance and a diamagnetic transition appear at 29 ± 1 K in 11 of the 14 samples; the remaining 3 contain an impurity phase identified by X-ray diffraction. An independent group reproduced the transition in samples we sent them. We do not claim the mechanism is unconventional; the data are also consistent with conventional pairing. Raw measurement files are available on request and in the supplementary data.

items.title: Sample: New superconductor confirmed, but it's no room-temperature miracle (test data)
items.text: A new paper (arXiv:2611.00001) reports a material that conducts electricity with zero resistance below about 29 kelvin, and a second lab has confirmed the result in 14 samples it tested. That is far colder than room temperature, and the authors say the finding does not mean practical applications are near. Physicists contacted for this story said the result is solid but modest, and whether the material's behaviour is unusual remains unclear.

items.title: Sample: Failure to reproduce reported room-temperature superconductivity in compound Q (test data)
items.text: Following the published synthesis route, we prepared 22 samples of compound Q in two independent laboratories. None showed zero resistance or a Meissner effect between 2 K and 400 K. The resistance drop near 380 K reported earlier coincides with a structural transition of a copper sulfide impurity, which we identified in 19 of our samples. We cannot rule out that a different synthesis produces a superconducting phase.

items.title: Sample: Room-temperature superconductor will transform civilization (test data)
items.text: Scientists at Sample Labs have achieved the holy grail of physics: a superconductor that works at room temperature and normal pressure. This incredible discovery will revolutionize energy, transportation and computing overnight. Lossless power lines and levitating trains are now just around the corner. History has been made.

items.title: Sample: Compound Z is a room-temperature superconductor (test data)
items.text: We prepared one sample of compound Z. A video shows a small fragment partially levitating above a magnet. This proves compound Z is a room-temperature superconductor, the first in history, and opens a new era for physics.

items.title: Sample: Batteries are about to make oil obsolete (test data)
items.text: Solid-state batteries are already here, and every carmaker will switch to them within two years. Charging will take a minute and cars will go a thousand miles. Most of the industry knows it and is just waiting to announce. Each generation of cells doubles the last, and the trend compounds. Oil will soon be obsolete. It is only a matter of time.

items.title: Sample: Employment effects of a regional minimum wage increase: a difference-in-differences study (test data)
items.text: We compare 412 counties that raised the minimum wage with 398 neighbouring counties that did not, using administrative payroll records for 2018 to 2025. Teen employment changed by -0.4% relative to the comparison group (95% CI, -1.9 to 1.1), and average earnings of low-wage workers rose 6.2%. Pre-trends were parallel in the four years before the increase. Our estimates may not generalize to larger increases or to national policy. Replication code and data extracts are publicly available.

items.title: Sample: Minimum wage rise lifted pay with little effect on jobs, study finds (test data)
items.text: A working paper (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.004) comparing about 800 counties found that a regional minimum wage increase raised low-wage workers' pay by about 6% without a measurable drop in teen jobs. The authors note the increase was modest, and the study does not show what a much larger national increase would do. Other economists said the design is strong but cautioned that effects may take longer than the study period to appear.

items.title: Sample: A cash transfer pilot had no detectable effect on labour supply (test data)
items.text: In a randomized pilot, 1,600 households received monthly transfers and 1,600 comparison households did not. After two years, hours worked differed by 0.3 hours per week (95% CI, -0.8 to 1.4). We find no effect on labour supply. The pilot was small relative to a national programme, and effects in local labour markets with many recipients may differ.

items.title: Sample: New economic plan guarantees prosperity for everyone (test data)
items.text: The Sample Institute's bold new plan will end poverty forever and guarantee unprecedented growth for every citizen. Economists everywhere agree this is the most brilliant policy ever devised. Within a year, every household will be wealthier than ever before. Prosperity is now inevitable.

items.title: Sample: Four-day weeks double productivity (test data)
items.text: We asked managers at 5 firms whether productivity improved after moving to a four-day week. All five said yes. This shows that four-day weeks double productivity and every company in the economy should adopt them immediately.

items.title: Sample: The recession is already here (test data)
items.text: The recession is already here, whatever the official numbers say. Every indicator that matters is pointing down, and most economists will admit it soon. Housing will collapse next, then jobs. Each month makes it worse and the pressure compounds. Anyone still optimistic will be proven wrong within the year. It is inevitable now.

items.title: Sample: Does a momentum strategy survive trading costs? Evidence from 30 years of returns (test data)
items.text: We test a momentum strategy on 30 years of monthly returns for 4,100 stocks, estimating returns net of trading costs from actual bid-ask spreads. Gross returns of 0.71% per month fall to 0.18% after costs (t = 1.4), which is not statistically significant. Results hold across subperiods and in an out-of-sample test on 1,900 international stocks. Limitations include the absence of short-selling constraints in our cost model. Code and data sources are documented in the appendix.

items.title: Sample: Popular trading strategy loses its edge after costs, study says (test data)
items.text: A study of 30 years of stock returns (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.005) found that a well-known momentum strategy earns about 0.7% a month on paper, but only about 0.2% after realistic trading costs, too little to rule out luck. The authors say they did not model every real-world constraint, and the result has not been tested on cryptocurrencies. Other researchers said whether some investors can still profit from it remains an open question.

items.title: Sample: Fund manager skill does not persist: evidence from 2,600 funds (test data)
items.text: We follow 2,600 actively managed funds over 2005 to 2025. Funds in the top quintile of returns in one five-year window were no more likely than chance to be in the top quintile in the next (21.3% versus 20% expected; p = 0.41). We find no evidence of persistent skill. Our sample excludes funds that closed within a year, which may bias results slightly upward.

items.title: Sample: SampleCoin guaranteed to 100x by year end (test data)
items.text: SampleCoin is the next revolution in money and is guaranteed to rise 100x by the end of the year. Early holders are already millionaires. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and the banks are terrified. Don't miss out: the moon is inevitable and the old financial system is finished.

items.title: Sample: A simple rule that beats the market every time (test data)
items.text: We back-tested a moving-average rule on one stock over six months and it beat the index every month. This proves the rule beats the market consistently and investors should use it for all their savings.

items.title: Sample: Real estate only goes up (test data)
items.text: House prices only go up, and every serious investor already knows it. Rates will fall soon and prices will jump again. Most people who wait will be priced out forever. Each year compounds the gains and nothing can stop the trend. Buying now is the only rational choice, and it will always be.

items.title: Sample: A preregistered multi-site replication of the ego-depletion effect (test data)
items.text: Following a preregistered protocol, 23 laboratories tested 2,141 participants. The pooled effect of the depletion task on later persistence was d = 0.04 (95% CI, -0.07 to 0.15), much smaller than the original estimate of d = 0.62. Effects did not differ by site. We cannot rule out effects under different task instructions. All materials, data and analysis code are on a public repository.

items.title: Sample: Famous willpower effect shrinks to almost nothing in large replication (test data)
items.text: A large replication involving 23 labs and more than 2,100 volunteers (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.006) found that a famous willpower effect was close to zero, far smaller than first reported. The researchers say other versions of the task have not been tested, so the idea is not fully ruled out. Psychologists not involved called the study careful, while noting it remains unclear why the original result was so large.

items.title: Sample: Brief mindset intervention did not improve grades: a randomized trial in 64 schools (test data)
items.text: We randomized 9,200 students in 64 schools to a 45-minute mindset session or a control session. End-of-year grades did not differ (difference 0.01 grade points; 95% CI, -0.03 to 0.05). The intervention did not improve grades overall. Effects among lower-achieving students were imprecise and our study was not powered for subgroups.

items.title: Sample: One simple trick rewires your brain for success (test data)
items.text: A revolutionary new technique from Sample Mind will rewire your brain in just five minutes a day. Users become happier, smarter and more successful almost immediately. Scientists are amazed. This life-changing method is guaranteed to transform anyone who tries it.

items.title: Sample: Power posing doubles confidence (test data)
items.text: Twelve students held a power pose for two minutes and then rated their confidence. Confidence ratings were higher than they expected. This demonstrates that power posing doubles confidence and should be taught in every school.

items.title: Sample: Screens are rewiring a generation (test data)
items.text: Smartphones have already rewired the brains of an entire generation. Every teacher sees it, and most parents know it too. Attention spans will keep shrinking until reading disappears. Each new app makes it worse and the damage compounds. Soon nobody under twenty will be able to focus at all. It is inevitable.

items.title: Sample: Ultra-processed food intake and weight gain: a controlled feeding study (test data)
items.text: In a crossover feeding study, 40 adults lived on a metabolic ward and ate an ultra-processed or a minimally processed diet for two weeks each, in random order. Participants ate 412 kcal more per day on the ultra-processed diet (95% CI, 236 to 588) and gained 0.9 kg. Diets were matched for presented calories, sugar, fat, fibre and macronutrients. The study was short and the sample small, so long-term effects are unknown.

items.title: Sample: Processed diet led people to eat more in a tightly controlled study (test data)
items.text: In a small but tightly controlled study (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.007), 40 volunteers ate about 400 more calories a day when given ultra-processed food than when given minimally processed meals. The researchers stress that the study lasted only four weeks and did not show long-term health effects. Nutrition scientists said the design is unusually rigorous, but whether the effect holds outside a lab remains unclear.

items.title: Sample: Daily egg consumption and cholesterol: a randomized trial (test data)
items.text: We randomized 520 adults to eat two eggs a day or none for 12 weeks. LDL cholesterol changed by 0.05 mmol/L between groups (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.14), not a meaningful difference. Eating eggs did not raise LDL cholesterol in this population. Participants with diabetes were excluded, so results may not apply to them.

items.title: Sample: Superfood powder melts fat overnight (test data)
items.text: Sample Nutrition's miracle superfood powder melts fat while you sleep. Customers are losing ten pounds a week without changing anything. This incredible formula is guaranteed to work for everyone and doctors don't want you to know about it. Order now before it sells out.

items.title: Sample: Celery juice cures inflammation (test data)
items.text: Seven volunteers drank celery juice each morning for ten days and said they felt less inflamed. This proves celery juice cures inflammation and it should replace anti-inflammatory medicines.

items.title: Sample: Seed oils are poisoning everyone (test data)
items.text: Seed oils are already behind most modern disease, and every honest doctor knows it. Within a few years they will be banned. Most of the food supply is contaminated and the damage compounds every year. Soon everyone will cook with animal fat again. It is only a matter of time. The truth is inevitable.
